questions.title: Kitchen and restaurant operations; Hygiene, safety and security

subQuestions.questionText: Study the adapted media statement about cholera (Public urged to adhere to cholera precautionary measures following first death; a patient died after profuse watery diarrhoea; 12 close contacts traced, two of whom are restaurant staff). Name THREE symptoms, other than watery diarrhoea, that the contacts could experience. (Refer to the source in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3:
• Nausea
• Vomiting
• Severe/rapid dehydration / severe water loss
• Blue death / death
• Rapid heart rate
• Dry mucous membrane / dry mouth
• Muscle cramps / stomach cramps / stomach pain / upset stomach
• Low blood pressure / dizziness

subQuestions.questionText: Motivate why the restaurant is not at risk to transmit the disease.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4:
• The establishment uses a proper sanitation system / clean / uncontaminated water
• The health board assured the restaurant they can continue / if there was a problem they would have shut it down / hygiene practices adhere to safety standards
• Staff ensure that food is covered at all times
• Staff use clean / uncontaminated / treated water to wash fruit and vegetables
• Restaurant provides treated / purified / bottled water for drinking
• Staff only serve cooked fish and shellfish
• Staff ensure food is cooked thoroughly
• Staff wash / sanitise hands often with antiseptic soap before and during food preparation
• Clean / sanitise work areas and surfaces regularly
• The two people did not contract the disease at the restaurant

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the people who are most at risk of contracting the disease.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3:
• People living in areas with poor sanitary systems and unsafe water supply / rural areas
• People with malnutrition
• People living with someone who has the disease
• People eating shellfish and vegetables from contaminated water
• Children / elderly
• People with low stomach acid levels
• People with weakened immune systems / people with HIV and AIDS

subQuestions.questionText: Study the guest survey below for TAMM Restaurant (Results from guest survey, 15 November 2023). Ratings: Quality of the food = 4; Waiting time for the meal = 1; Time it took to be seated = 4; Taking of the food order = 3; Professionalism and efficiency of staff = 3; Overall excellent service = 1; Recommendation of restaurant to friends = 1. Rating scale: 1 = Poor; 2 = Acceptable; 3 = Good; 4 = Excellent. Analyse the impact that the positive and negative results may have on TAMM Restaurant and its profitability. (Refer to the source in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Positive results (Any 2):
• The feedback is good / positive; profitability will increase
• Guests will return for the food / good reviews / quality of food rated excellent
• Guests received well-prepared food / willing to pay for good quality food
• Taking of the food order rated good
• Guests seated promptly / felt welcomed / time to be seated rated excellent
• Staff created a good impression / professionalism and efficiency rated good
AND Negative results (Any 2):
• The feedback is bad / negative
• Guests will not recommend restaurant / recommendation rated poor / negative word of mouth
• Guests may not return / fewer customers
• Profit will be reduced / less profit
• Overall service rated poor / customer care compromised
• Waiting time very long / rated poor / guests don't like to wait
(2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Study the scenario: Due to load-shedding, Five-star Fish Shop is struggling to control stock. A wholesale truck delivered 10 boxes of fish cakes; with computers offline the storekeeper drew up a manual stock control card and incorrectly captured five boxes. On the computerised stock control card: Description = Haddock fish cakes 300 g; Date = 22/11/2023; Stock received = (a); Price per unit = R45,99; Stock on hand = 12; Balance = (b). Rectify information (a) and (b) that the storekeeper must record on the computerised stock card. (Refer to the source in the question paper.)
Briefly explain how computers are beneficial for stock control systems at Five-star Fish Shop.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4:
• Help to manage stock / simplify the stock receiving process
• The process is less time consuming / quicker
• Fewer errors / more accurate / less human error
• Reduces paperwork / environmentally friendly / reduces carbon footprint
• Control the flow of stock / tracks movement / quantity of stock at any time / subtracts automatically as stock is issued
• Missing stock detected quickly
• Stock control can be carried out often
• System reflects detail of stock automatically
• Reduces wastage e.g. preventing issuing extra stock
• Total cost / price per unit recorded instantly
• Stock sheets can be printed / printed alphabetically for easier stocktaking
• Easy to update and reorganise information
• Improves communication between departments
• Reduce or prevent theft
• Fewer people required to do stocktaking
• Stock records kept safely with passwords

subQuestions.questionText: Study the following choice of dishes for a menu — Hors d'oeuvre: Sushi; Entrée: Grilled Bacon and Cheese Mushrooms; Main course: Schnitzels served with Potato Croquettes; Dessert: Chocolate Mousse. Name TWO anaphylactic reactions a guest can display after eating the grilled bacon and cheese mushrooms.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2:
• Swelling of the tongue
• Swelling of the throat
• Heart palpitations
• Suffocation / difficulty breathing
• Blood pressure drops
• Pulse is weak / fast
• Skin rash / hives
• Nausea / vomiting
• May lead to death

subQuestions.questionText: Evaluate the choice of food dishes for a formal four-course menu.
subQuestions.memoText:
1 mark for stating Good or Bad + 4 appropriate reasons (5):
Good:
• Variety of dishes / different proteins (fish, schnitzel) / different vegetables
• Basic ingredients not repeated
• Variety of colours
• Variety of flavours
• Variety of temperature (hot and cold food)
• Variety of cooking methods (grilled, fried, boiled, steamed)
• Dishes suitable for each course of a formal dinner
• Dishes correspond with expected portion sizes
OR Bad:
• No variety of texture (mostly soft)
• No contrast of colour (mostly brown)
• No variety in shape (mostly round)
• Too many starchy items (rice, potatoes, crumbs)
• Limited nutritional balance / few fresh vegetables
• Very rich / fatty food (bacon, cheese, oil, cream)
• No sauce / gravy / vegetables in main course
• Two deep-fried items in the main course

subQuestions.questionText: The choice of dishes is unsuitable for a guest with diabetes. Motivate your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4:
• Too much refined starch e.g. rice, potatoes and crumbs — avoid the mashed potatoes in croquettes / avoid schnitzel because of the crumbing
• Too much sugar — avoid the chocolate mousse
• Too much fat in the menu (chocolate mousse, bacon, cheese) — exclude the fatty dishes / avoid frying / decrease total and saturated fat / avoid schnitzel and croquettes that are fried, rather air fry or grill
• Processed meats included — avoid the bacon

subQuestions.questionText: Study the pictures of a croquembouche and gougères. Differentiate between the choux pastry puffs used in croquembouche and gougères. Tabulate your answer under the headings CROQUEMBOUCHE and GOUGÈRES. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 valid contrast per column (2):
CROQUEMBOUCHE — plain choux pastry puffs / no flavouring; sweet; lighter/crispier texture; filled with cream, crème pâtissière or chantilly cream; glazed or dusted with icing sugar; covered with spun sugar.
GOUGÈRES — flavoured with cheese; savoury; heavier/more moist because of the cheese; filled with a savoury filling; not dusted with icing sugar / sprinkled with chopped herbs, grated cheese or paprika; not covered with spun sugar.

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest how the baked choux pastry puffs for the croquembouche can be stored if prepared two days before assembling.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2:
• Place in an airtight container or bag / cover with plastic wrap
• Can last 3 days at room temperature / in a dry place
• Can be frozen
• Store without filling

subQuestions.questionText: Explain THREE possible reasons why the baked gougères could be heavy and greasy.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3:
• Overcooking of the water and butter / boiled for too long
• Too much water evaporated / too little steam
• The oven was not hot enough
• The batter contained too much fat / butter / too much cheese added
• Incorrect proportion of water to fat/butter (not 2:1) / incorrect measuring
• Too little egg to emulsify the fat / butter

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the preparation of the spun sugar used to garnish the croquembouche.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2:
• Spun sugar is prepared by boiling a sugar syrup / melting sugar until it caramelises / until golden or light brown
• It is made by rapidly flicking / quick moving of the caramelised sugar using a cut whisk / fork
• It can be spun over dowels / wooden spoons / on a table to create long, fine hairy threads of sugar

subQuestions.questionText: Study the picture of hot smoking. Describe the process of hot smoking. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1:
• The meat is placed in a smoker / closed container / space where it is exposed to smoke from burning wood chips, dried tea leaves or rice
• The meat is cooked during smoking at above 52 °C

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the benefits of hot smoking.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4:
• Smoking preserves the food / lengthens / increases shelf life
• Retards growth of micro-organisms
• Accelerates / quickens the drying process
• Prevents enzymatic browning
• Salt retards the growth of micro-organisms
• Food is cooked / ready to eat
• Slows down rancidification / fat will not go off quickly
• Adds a smoky taste / enhances the flavour
• Appearance is more appealing

subQuestions.questionText: Name THREE types of food that can be preserved using hot smoking.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3 (1 mark for either the food group Meat/Fish/Chicken/Fruit OR examples):
• Meat: beef / pork / lamb / ham / sausages / ribs / salami / bacon / gammon / brisket
• Chicken / turkey
• Fish: salmon / trout / snoek
• Fruit: mangoes / pineapples / apricots / peaches
• Paprika / tomatoes / egg plant / brinjal

subQuestions.questionText: List the benefits of consuming plant-based meals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4:
• High in plant protein
• Low in fat / low in kilojoules
• Cholesterol free
• Natural source of fibre / high in fibre
• Rich in antioxidants
• Cheaper than animal products / substitutes for animal proteins
• Rich in complex carbohydrates
• Low in glycaemic index
• Excellent source of nutrients / vitamins / minerals
• No hormones / antibiotics
• Limits the negative effect on the environment / lessens carbon footprint
• Helps to prevent lifestyle diseases / healthier

subQuestions.questionText: Predict why Plant Café might not be as popular among flexitarians as it is among vegans.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the list of hors d'oeuvres below and choose TWO items that are NOT suitable for the Plant Café's cocktail platters. Motivate EACH item chosen. LIST OF HORS D'OEUVRES: rissoles; foie gras; salsa; crudités; tofu skewers; hummus; fish nuggets.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the pictures of sweet short crust pastry (A: TECHNIQUE; B: SHRUNKEN PASTRY; C: FRUIT TARTLET). Motivate why the utensils, equipment and ingredients must be kept ice cold when preparing short crust pastry. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)

• Leg

subQuestions.questionText: Identify and describe the cooking method used when cooking the mutton.
subQuestions.memoText:
Name of cooking method (Any 1): Stewing / braising.
Description (Any 2):
• Brown / sear meat in a little oil
• Mutton simmers slowly in a covered potjie / three-legged pot / saucepan in a small amount of liquid below boiling point (85–99 °C)
• Bubbles rise to the surface without bursting

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO quality characteristics of the fat and texture of mutton. Tabulate your answers under the headings FAT and TEXTURE.

TEXTURE (Any 2): smooth; fine grain; firm and not dry.
(4)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the loss of sarcoplasm can be prevented during the preparation and cooking of the meat cuts for the potjiekos dish.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3:
• Before cooking do not immerse meat in water or wash it because nutrients are lost
• The flavoursome components are removed when meat is washed
• Meat must be salted after cooking; salt extracts meat juices / do not salt meat before cooking
• Sear or seal meat before cooking
• Meat must be thawed correctly to limit losses caused by dripping
• Thaw meat in the refrigerator
• Avoid cooking the meat at too high or too low temperatures

subQuestions.questionText: Read the information about the Mpumzale Wedding (50 guests, 24 August 2023, 14:00 to 21:00). Costs — Food R4 500,00; Wedding cake R1 200,00; Beverages R3 000,00; Music and entertainment R1 500,00; Large tent and Tiffany chairs R4 500,00; Laser-cut name cards R600,00; Flowers R500,00; Casual staff: Waiters x 5 @ R100,00 per hour. Calculate the labour cost for the duration of the function. Show ALL formulas and calculations. (Refer to the source in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Labour cost = amount per hour x number of hours x number of waiters
= R100 per hour x 7 hours x 5 waiters
= R3 500
(3)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify TWO items that form part of the overhead costs.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2:
• Music and entertainment
• Large tent
• Tiffany chairs
• Laser-cut name cards
• Flowers

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total cost of the wedding. Show ALL formulas and calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total cost = Cost of food and beverage + cost of hiring/overheads + labour cost
= (R4 500 + R1 200 + R3 000) + (R1 500 + R4 500 + R600 + R500) + (R3 500)
= R8 700 + R7 100 + R3 500
= R19 300
(No brackets: only 1 mark) (4)

• Special prices / discounts / packages / loyalty programmes
• Use visual marketing tools to attract potential customers
• Use electronic marketing / social media / internet / update website
• Host competitions

subQuestions.questionText: Name and describe TWO non-revenue-generating areas in an accommodation establishment that contribute to an increase in income, because of the positive image it creates.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 areas named + described (2+2) (4):
• Reception/front office: where guests make first contact when booking / heart of the establishment / good first impressions create a positive image
• Housekeeping: responsible for cleaning the hotel; clean rooms and common areas encourage guests to return
• Laundry: responsible for washing, ironing and dry cleaning linen; clean linen leads to satisfied returning guests
• Maintenance: responsible for renovating, gardening and repairs; well-maintained buildings/gardens create a positive image
• Security: protects people and assets; guests feel safe and consider returning
• Human resources: employing/training qualified staff creates a good image

subQuestions.questionText: List FOUR general requirements for an on-consumption (on the premises) liquor licence.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4:
• No person under the age of 18 may be served alcohol
• Minors will not be granted a liquor licence
• Adequate guest toilet facilities for males and females must be provided on or near the premises
• Ordinary meals shall be available on the premises during the hours that liquor is sold
• Liquor may be sold on any day between 10:00 and 02:00, provided that on 'closed days' (Sundays, Good Friday and Christmas Day) liquor may only be sold to a person taking an ordinary meal
• No liquor may be supplied or sold to a person who is drunk
• All liquor bought on the premises must be consumed on the premises
• A person may bring their own liquor onto the premises upon which a 'corkage fee' is charged; such liquor must be consumed on the premises
• It is illegal to add any liquids such as water to the liquor in a bottle / adulteration is illegal
• A bankrupt or unrehabilitated person will not receive a licence
• The applicant / spouse should not have a criminal record
• Applicant must be compliant with SARS tax laws

subQuestions.questionText: Study the image showing a cocktail-making method (shaking). Describe the general rules for preparing cocktails when using the method in the picture above. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 5:
• Follow the recipe carefully
• Use good quality products
• Accurate measurements are important when mixing drinks / use a tot measure
• A cocktail that contains cream, fruit juice or eggs should be shaken
• Do not overfill the shaker
• Make sure the shaker is sealed properly
• Never shake effervescent drinks
• Ice should be clear and clean
• Serve in chilled glasses
• Place the ice in the glass / shaker
• Shake well / from left to right / for about 10 seconds
• Open the shaker carefully to prevent spills
• Use a strainer when pouring the drink
• Don't overfill the glass
• Finish off with garnishing (straw, cherry, etc.)

subQuestions.questionText: State FIVE guidelines to follow when setting up a venue for a formal function.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 5:
• The venue must be set up according to the organiser's suggestions
• Create a pleasant / relaxed / formal atmosphere for the guest
• The colour scheme should be warm and welcoming
• Furniture should be durable and comfortable
• Know the number of covers / guests
• Choose music that enhances the theme / not too loud
• Use different types of lighting e.g. natural / low lighting / candles
• Ensure the temperature is comfortable / not too cold or hot
• The room must be well ventilated
• Have beautiful plants in the background
• Interior and décor / flowers should match the theme / ensure décor blends
• Correct positioning of tables and chairs for easy flow / movement
• Align tables and chairs / arrange in a pattern
• Make sure tables and chairs are not wobbly / levelled
• Ensure enough tables, chairs, cutlery, crockery / glasses
• Ensure the venue and equipment are clean

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the guests would be greeted and welcomed in the restaurant.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4:
• Maître d'hôtel / head waiter should acknowledge new guests within 30 seconds of entering the restaurant
• Maître d'hôtel greets guests in a professional / polite / friendly / welcoming way
• Make eye contact
• Check the reservation / ask if they have a booking / note the name of the host
• Maître d'hôtel introduces guests to the waiter
• The waiter greets in a friendly manner
• Do not leave customers at the door, always ask them to follow you / show guests to their table
• Address the host in his/her preferred language / address as Sir or Mam / by surname as it appears in the booking
• If the maître d'hôtel is not available, another waiter / manager must step in and receive the guests at the door

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how you would handle a guest who flirts with a waitron during restaurant service.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3:
• Be polite and friendly without being familiar / be professional
• Be attentive, but do not respond to the flirting
• Ask them politely to stop
• Serve the meal as soon as possible
• Ask the maître d'hôtel or manager to assist
• Get another waiter of a different gender to serve the table
• If the guest continues, ask the guest to leave
• If the guest refuses, call security to escort the guest out of the restaurant
